comments.author: claude
comments.text:
hjkl gaps nm handles itself, found in the spike (nmr-ye9.1) and the skeleton (nmr-b19.1). Each has a workaround and tests in src/tui/editor.rs; verify them here and fill what is left.
- Deletes reach the clipboard hook as well as yanks; only y may hit the system clipboard (SPEC 10 register rule). Still on DefaultHost; the real Host comes with the clipboard story.
- Insert-mode Left at column 0 and Right at end of line do not wrap; nm intercepts.
- Autopair, autoindent, smartindent and comment continuation are on by default; autopair only turns off through settings_mut().
- A buffer ending in \n has an unreachable phantom last row. nm stores an extra trailing \n and drops that row when reading lines back. Deleting every line removes the newline; nm restores it without an undo step. Redo can land on the phantom row; nm pulls the cursor back.
- Insert-mode End, Up, Down use normal-mode column rules; nm fixes the column after the move.
- / ? q : start search, macro and command prompts inside the engine; nm intercepts them in normal and visual mode. : is held until nmr-b19.4.
- Tab, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P are swallowed until the completion story.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Landed in 9b0792c. hjkl quirks found and worked around in src/tui/keys.rs and editor.rs (each has a test):
- F and T after an operator are inclusive in hjkl, so dF( also deleted the cursor char; nm redoes the range. Open gap: . after dF( repeats a character count instead of searching again.
- Cursor can land one past end of line in normal mode after J with an empty line, after . repeating A, and after a visual delete that ends the line; nm clamps.
- hjkl records an undo step on entering insert mode and for no-op edits; nm drops those. Arrow keys split an insert session into several undo steps; nm merges.
- v in charwise visual and V in linewise visual did not leave visual; nm handles.
- Y is y$ as in nvim. T with the target adjacent counts as not found. R reports itself as insert mode.
- Ctrl+D/Ctrl+U and H M L use hjkl's own screen model, which nm does not sync, so they are not in doc/keys.md.
- hjkl's undo_stack_len is undocumented; nm reads the count through hjkl_buffer::View.
Intentional departures from Go (no Go test conflicts): ygg and yk move the cursor to the range start as in vim; $ then j keeps the cursor at line ends as in vim.
Perf: the app re-read all lines from the editor on every key (~19 ms per key at 210 lines, debug). Now re-reads only when text may have changed; test suite 12 s to 0.2 s.

- Quit guard `E37` for a modified named file; session mode quits and auto-saves (skip when all lines blank).

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Go side is tests/parity/goeval/main.go compiled with a go build -overlay into the Go module (nothing written to the Go repo; GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly). run.sh generates tmp/parity/overlay.json; NM_GO_REPO overrides the Go checkout. Masks live in a parity-masks block in doc/parity.md; each masked line must differ in exactly its declared class (jq check), so new differences still fail. 7 intentional difference classes, no Rust bugs found: error-message (Go drops tokenizer text; unary-minus errors also show error not syntax), rounding (1.999), non-finite (Go prints -9,223,372,036,854,775,808Inf), range-error, big-int (Go goes through int64 so >= 2^63 prints garbage), unicode-message (Go names one byte of a multibyte char), unicode-space (Go reads NBSP as letter+space, giving undef where Rust gives 8). Go-repo story to file: add nm eval with the same JSON lines, then drop the overlay.

title: Allow variable names that start with a digit
description: Today a token starting with a digit is always a number, so 2024_rent is a syntax error. Proposed rule: a token that starts with a digit is a name if it contains a character that cannot be part of a number, otherwise a number. So 2x is a name, 2,000 is a number, 2,000x is an error. Change the identifier-start check in src/lang/tokenizer.rs and the assignment-target check in src/lang/line.rs; add spec cases for 2024_rent=1200, 2x, 2,000x, and the live-typing sequence 2024 -> 2024_ -> 2024_rent=1200. Update README 'The pad' and doc/design/language.md. Cost: names like 2024_rent*2 are harder to read than rent_2024*2; no mainstream language allows this.

description: Read the active Omarchy palette so nm matches the desktop theme. title: Reload the theme live when it changes
description: nm reads the theme once at startup, so an Omarchy theme switch needs a restart. Poll the modification time of the theme sources (nm theme.toml, Omarchy colors.toml and theme.name) from the event loop and reload on change. No hook required.
close_reason: Event loop polls theme file mtimes every 500 ms and reloads on change; verified live against an Omarchy switch to catppuccin and back

comments.author: claude
comments.text: theme::Watch stamps each source path (mtime, len) and reports a change; the loop uses event::poll(500 ms) instead of a blocking read and reloads on a changed stamp. No hook needed; also catches edits to ~/.config/nm/theme.toml. Omarchy rm -rf + mv of current/theme guarantees a new mtime.

title: Spike: choose the vim editor crate by building the nm layout on each
description:
One-day spike: pick the vim editor crate by building the nm layout on top of each candidate and keeping the one that lets us own rendering.

## Candidates
- `hjkl-engine` + `hjkl-buffer` (engine and buffer separated from rendering; pre-1.0)
- `vimltui` (operators, text objects, dot repeat, registers, search; owns state per editor)
- `edtui` (most popular; EditorState/EditorView split; syntect highlighting)
Check each on crates.io/docs.rs for current version, maintenance, and license before starting.

## What to build (throwaway, in `spike/<crate>/` dirs, not `src/`)
For each candidate, a tiny ratatui app that:
1. Holds three lines: `income=5000`, `expenses = 3000`, `income - expenses`.
2. Renders OUR line content (gutter `" 1 │ "`, our own token styling, and a fake dimmed ghost `me` after the cursor on line 1) in the left 60% and a results column on the right. The crate must NOT draw the text; we draw it, the crate owns buffer/cursor/modes/motions.
3. Feeds keys headless (no terminal) in a test: `dw`, `ct=`, `3j`, `u`, `cw` + text + Esc, `v` + `l` + `y`, and asserts buffer and cursor. Record which of these each crate supports.
4. Places the native terminal cursor (bar in insert, block in normal) from the crate's cursor position.
5. Checks unicode: insert `é`, move left, delete; cursor column must be in characters.

## Deliverable
- `docs/spike-editor-core.md`: a table of crate × (headless drive, own rendering, motions supported, counts, undo, visual modes, text objects, unicode, maintenance), and the decision with reasons.
- CLAUDE.md "Decisions" updated with the chosen crate and version.
- The spike code deleted or left under `spike/` excluded from the workspace; it must not be in `src/`.
If no crate allows owning the rendering while driving keys headless, say so and recommend "write our own motion engine in Rust" with an estimate; do not pick a crate that forces its view on us.

## Acceptance criteria
